title: ColoQ (CRC-digital-twin): mechanistic digital twin for colorectal cancer molecular subtyping (CMS1–4) via Hopfield attractor dynamics on an RT-qPCR panel
description:
ColoQ is a mechanistic digital twin of colorectal cancer that models the four Consensus Molecular Subtypes (CMS1–CMS4) as attractors of a continuous Hopfield-type network. Patterns are calibrated against real labeled cohorts (GSE39582) and validated against external cohorts and survival outcomes. The model is designed to run on a 10-gene panel measurable by RT-qPCR alone (no ddPCR, NGS or exosome sequencing), and includes a longitudinal post-surgical prognosis module and counterfactual treatment simulation.

The release includes the full pipeline (calibration, external validation, stratified Cox analyses and diagnostics, dynamical diagnostics, Modern Hopfield V1/V2 comparison), a Streamlit web interface (also available in the browser via GitHub Pages: https://danpc11.github.io/CRC-digital-twin/), a Docker image and single-file executables.

Research tool only — not a medical device or a validated clinical decision aid. Licensed for noncommercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0).
